title: Newly discovered immune hubs in our skull may keep our brain healthy | New Scientist
description: We may have clusters of immune cells at the back of our skull that help ward off conditions like brain cancer
author: Carissa Wong

title: AI could offer a shortcut for designing more efficient airplane wings | New Scientist
description: AI agents devised a way to reduce friction of an airplane wing model even without access to a costly computer simulation
author: Karmela Padavic-Callaghan

title: Supercentenarians have hypervigilant immune systems that fight off cancer | New Scientist
description: People aged 110 or older seem to have a disproportionately high number of immune cells that fight off cancer and infections
author: James Woodford

title: 5-year-old brain organoids can sense the passing of time | New Scientist
description: Brain organoids have been grown and studied for five years, the longest time to date, and their activity suggests they had a sense of time going by
author: Carissa Wong

title: We may now know which neurons dictate when it is time to go to sleep | New Scientist
description: Two clusters of neurons in the brains of mice seem to create the drive to get some shuteye, potentially hinting at a new target for sleep disorder treatments
author: Chris Simms

title: World may warm by 25 per cent more than current projections suggest | New Scientist
description: Official projections for how much the world will warm are already catastrophic, and now it appears they significantly underestimate future warming
author: Michael Le Page
